item.title: Building a better Bugbot
item.description:
This means that the number of resolved bugs per PR has more than doubled, from roughly 0. Resolution rate directly answers whether Bugbot is finding real issues that engineers fix. #Hill-climbing Defining resolution rate changed how we built Bugbot.

HN Discussion

Read Original Article

Top 2 Comments:

agent013:

The biggest problem with LLM reviews for me is not false positives, but authority. Younger devs are used to accepting bot comments as the ultimate truth, even when they are clearly questionable

skrebbel:

Few things give me more dread than reviewing the mediocre code written by an overconfident LLM, but arguing in a PR with an overconfident LLM that its review comments are wrong is up there.

item.title: Show HN: BGP Scout – BGP Network Browser
item.description:
Access comprehensive Border Gateway Protocol data from thousands of networks worldwide Access BGP routing changes as they happen with our live feed system Analyze routing trends with our comprehensive historical database Integrate BGP data directly into your applications with our robust API.

HN Discussion

Read Original Article

Top 4 Comments:

pjf:

I'd advise to first compare with:

- https://bgp.tools/ - https://bgproutes.io/ - https://bgp.he.net/ - https://radar.qrator.net/ - https://github.com/nttgin/BGPalerter

...all of which are (usually) free. IMHO you should have a competing product + money strategy before you continue. Many people have tried (and failed) to make money off BGP.

BTW, author of https://bgpipe.org/ here, an open-source BGP data tool

erinnh:

>What would make something like this actually useful in day-to-day work?

Monitoring of BGP Changes for ASNs.

The other stuff isn't something I really need a new tool for.

There are other tools by Ripe, HE and the like that already allow me to see historical data.

The only point at which I need actual up-to-date to the minute data is during incidents. Hence the monitoring.

eqvinox:

Sorry, too lazy to sign up just to try it out.

yesod:

I usually just grab the RIS data from RIPE
